source.title: Scaling Word2Vec on Big Corpus
source.authors: Bo-Fang Li; Aleksandr Drozd; Yuhe Guo; Tao Liu; S. Matsuoka; Xiao-Yong Du

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports effects on word-embedding benchmark scores, using a different outcome measure from train–test error.
record.gate_note: The batch-size sweep in W2V-Vanilla reports a qualitative change in embedding benchmark scores. Figure 13 does not provide recoverable values in the supplied text. W2V-CL is a separate training recipe that reports comparable benchmark performance to W2V-Vanilla; it is not a direct batch-size-only comparison.
record.test_reason: The study measures word-embedding quality and training speed, rather than held-out performance of image classifiers or language models as specified by V5. Its fixed-one-epoch batch sweep is relevant but measures a different construct. References to generalization gaps and sharp minima do not supply its own tests of those claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that W2V-CL permits larger batches without loss of embedding quality, trains roughly twice as fast as the reference implementation, and scales across GPUs. This conclusion concerns the complete revised recipe, rather than an isolated batch-size change or matched training-work comparison.
record.recipe_differences: W2V-CL changes sampling, iteration control, and update procedure relative to the original Word2Vec training approach. It is evaluated on word-embedding benchmarks, not train–test error.
record.method_sensitivity: For W2V-Vanilla, benchmark scores decline as batch size increases, with a faster decline above 1024. Context size also changes benchmark scores, but is outside the mapped claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: With one training epoch, W2V-Vanilla's similarity and analogy scores decrease across nine batch-size settings and 13 datasets, with a steeper decline above 1024. Numeric scores are unavailable in the supplied figure text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size can reduce intrinsic word-embedding quality under a fixed corpus-pass budget.

fits_no_version.finding: W2V-CL performs comparably to W2V-Vanilla on embedding benchmarks, outperforming it on 12 of 20 datasets. It changes sampling, update rules, and training work as well as batch size; Section 5.4 reports approximately 17.6 times as many operations for its selected configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A revised word-embedding training recipe can accommodate larger batches while preserving benchmark quality, with different training work.

record.problems: The batch-size results are reported in a figure without recoverable numeric values in the supplied text. The study evaluates embedding quality on intrinsic and downstream NLP benchmarks rather than train–test error or language-model held-out performance.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 13 reports the batch-size sweep qualitatively, but its values and individual batch conditions are not recoverable from the supplied text. No row was retained because the study does not report the train–test/generalization-gap outcome specified by V5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer differences in held-out performance under specified tuning budgets. The undocumented pilot preference for Adam supplies neither benchmark results nor tuning conditions.
Large-batch penalties and their recovery in image classifiers or language models. Embedding similarity and analogy scores do not measure the specified systems' held-out performance.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and removing weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures. Sharp minima are discussed as a possible explanation but not measured.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change V5 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. V5 requires held-out performance, not necessarily a train–test gap; the exclusion rests on the system and outcome mismatch. The batch sweep is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not a missing result. No version-specific verdicts are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
The study tests batch-size effects on word-embedding benchmark scores, but does not report train–test error or language-model held-out performance as specified by this version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
